title: Own recording pause, resume and retry through complete operations
what: Deepen the existing C# recording owner so the actual session and recording controls request complete pause, resume and explicit retry operations. The owner retains file completion, failure and release duties after a caller stops waiting, while preserving the already specified Rust recording content and interval behavior. This implements the whole-codebase Q1-Q3 ownership refinement to the existing native-recording work rather than rebuilding its projections.
criteria: Route production pause, resume, retry and initial recording preparation through named complete operations on one session-generation recording owner; ordinary callers no longer assemble native cutoff, writer completion, durable flush and handle-release steps or own operation leases.

Expose bounded immutable results/status and a read-only actual-release observation. Distinguish inactive/no-change, accepted work, successful save/pause, failed or incomplete recording, and resources still owned; cancelling observation does not cancel the accepted operation.

Preserve whole-selected-format preparation before transport startup, disabled recording behavior, interval eligibility, fresh parts without backfill, and cancellation before activation. A partial open never activates a subset; its original owner closes successful handles and leaves created files as already specified.

A successful Pause requires the ordered Rust cutoff, completion of accepted writes, durable flush and part close. Actual write/flush/close errors stop group admission without replay, guessed byte counts or damage to healthy terminal effects and replies.

Keep the 8 MiB group allowance, approximately one-second batching and ten-second pending-I/O no-progress policy. Idle time without pending I/O does not fail recording; issued and failed-but-owned buffers remain charged until actual completion.

Explicit Retry creates fresh part owners and numbers. Delayed opening or prior-part completion/failure cannot activate or mutate the replacement; unavailable existing cleanup capacity rejects or defers new preparation visibly without accumulating owners.

Exercise the ordinary production interface with real Rust semantics, independent expected log bytes, controlled blocked/partial/failed/late file I/O and time, plus real-file and recording-control integration. Preserve the native content cases from the related issues rather than replacing them with helper-count assertions.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q1-Q3: selected named recording operations and lifetime seam
Candidate 1 verification rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 15, 16; observation-cancellation portion of row 14

title: Finalize received recordings once without closing directional EOF ownership
what: Route receive EOF and disconnect through the same complete recording owner used for pause and retry. A peer ending its receive direction flushes the eligible received content once while preserving recording-part ownership and any permitted opposite-direction interaction; a later pause, disconnect or close shares that work instead of repeating it.
criteria: Add and use named complete receive-completion and disconnect-completion operations on the existing session-generation recording owner, preserving the distinction from Pause and final Close.

Apply source decoder/parser finalization and eligible Text tails once at their ordered receive cutoff; flush accepted work through that position while EOF retains part/session ownership and does not globally pause otherwise permitted local-echo recording. SSH local echo remains disabled.

Preserve reverse input where the transport permits it after receive EOF. Retained disconnected output remains usable, and EOF or recording completion never claims to release transport or retained-terminal ownership.
Repeated EOF, disconnect after EOF, pause after EOF and overlapping drains share admitted I/O and once-only terminal finalization while reporting each operation's own completion condition.

Complete only the required session ordering step from EOF/disconnect callbacks. Do not await aggregate close/session completion that depends on that callback, and retain observation and original-generation cleanup when a caller stops waiting.

Verify exact Raw/Text/Terminal bytes and file lifetime through real Rust/session paths for split source tails, EOF then permitted input, EOF followed by pause/disconnect, repeated facts, overlapping pause drains, failed flush and delayed old-generation completion.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q1-Q3: distinct EOF/disconnect meanings and overlapping completion
Candidate 1 verification rows 3, 4, 12, 15; EOF/overlap portions of row 11

title: Preserve recording work throughout close waiting and later loss decisions
what: Connect the existing tab/window closure workflow to the recording owner's protected close operation. Accepting closure immediately protects its pending log work, Continue waiting keeps that protection, and the same close remains able to accept a later explicit loss decision. The log-loss choice reflects recording work rather than unrelated transport cleanup.
criteria: Acceptance of explicit close joins or starts one recording close and protects its admitted work before waiting for an existing pause/EOF/disconnect drain, final cutoff, the five-second question or the user's answer. A prior completed I/O failure is not reversed.

Only unresolved recording work triggers the existing five-second log-loss choice. Transport-only cleanup does not trigger it; Continue waiting preserves the existing timer/choice without repeated prompts and prevents automatic ten-second abandonment.

Keep a later explicit close-with-unsaved-data action accessible on the same close owner. Forward that decision through the complete recording operation without a caller cleanup recipe or a new allowance; when required cleanup admission is unavailable, report it and preserve the pending wait.

Loss permission abandons only unissued work and requests cancellation of issued work where possible. Preserve issued buffers, file handles and charges until actual completion, including blocked synchronous flush; cleanup adoption and visual removal do not prove actual release.

Distinguish save success, incomplete/uncertain recording, pending release and cleanup adoption. A late loss answer cannot damage a completed save or another generation, and late completion cannot overwrite an established incomplete outcome with an unqualified save-success claim.

Repeated tab/window/bulk/automatic closure requests join existing recording work and decisions through the already specified closure owner. A missing view, cancelled observation or failed question presentation supplies no implicit loss permission and creates no cyclic completion wait.

Use localized English/Japanese presentation for any affected visible choice/status. Verify through real WPF closure and session/Rust recording paths with controlled blocked writes/flushes, clocks, actual I/O errors, late completion and cleanup-capacity pressure across both five- and ten-second thresholds.

Verify recording-versus-transport completion using the existing transport/session seam, including a completed log with transport cleanup still held. The close owner depends on the recording result and does not require the new transport interface to distinguish those outcomes.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q1-Q3: close protection, Continue waiting, later explicit loss and independent release
Candidate 1 verification rows 6-9, 11-14, 16; delayed failure/release portions of rows 10 and 15

title: Run Telnet sessions through complete terminal-payload transport operations
what: Introduce the accepted complete transport seam through the live Telnet connection path. The transport owns Telnet startup, negotiation, framing and geometry notifications; the terminal session receives ordered terminal payload and facts and retains input permission, local-echo policy, Rust processing and recording delivery. This is the exercised prefactoring path for migrating the other transports.
criteria: Bind one typed awaited receive consumer and access to current committed geometry before I/O. Use named Start, Send prepared input, Apply committed geometry and Disconnect operations with bounded status/results and separate actual-release observation; retain compatible existing paths for transports not yet migrated.

Prepare the session and required recording files before starting I/O. Telnet becomes ready on TCP availability without remote-login inference, credential retrieval or waiting for every option negotiation; repeated Start observes one attempt rather than reconnecting.

Move IAC/NVT conversion, option negotiation, NAWS representation and dedicated Telnet commands behind the transport. Preserve source/payload/fact order through fragmented IAC and CR state, including negotiated echo changes inside a mixed read. Raw contains de-framed payload before Rust decoding, never negotiation bytes.

Keep local-echo policy, encoded complete-unit interpretation, input permission and pacing in the session/Rust owners. Send reports rejected, accepted-unsent, definitely submitted complete units and any partial/uncertain suffix promptly enough for pacing/echo; do not replay input or echo partial units.

Consume one nonrecursive ordered callback at a time. Completion follows Rust processing, separately accounted recording admission or its narrow failure, bounded reply admission and release of the received allocation; it never waits for disk flush, painting or reply transmission. Account queued/in-flight payload and ordered metadata and keep protocol control/cancellation progress possible without holding locks or the session reducer across waits.

Apply current committed geometry without holding the reducer through startup or I/O. Distinguish supersession and notification failure without claiming remote rendering; preserve dedicated Telnet actions without introducing a universal capability collection.

Deliver EOF/closed through the session-owned receive-cutoff and recording-lifecycle entry points; the transport consumer never owns file finalization or awaits its aggregate completion. Retain a compatible session bridge during migration so the recording owner can be deepened independently. Directional recording-part retention is accepted and verified by R2, not reimplemented in this transport slice.

Distinguish directional EOF, final closed facts and transport release. Disconnect joins one shutdown, observation cancellation leaves accepted work owned, and attempt cancellation prevents activation while already-admitted delivery settles in its original generation. Consumer failure after partial application causes independent observable failure without redelivery or a required final callback.

Verify the live session/Rust/log path with independent Telnet bytes, controlled fragmentation/echo-order/partial-write/slow-consumer/late-I/O cases and real loopback-peer coverage. Source extraction alone or a forwarding wrapper that leaves framing in the session does not satisfy this ticket.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q4-Q6: selected interface and terminal/transport responsibility split, Telnet production adoption
Candidate 2 verification rows 1, 3, 6-13 as applicable to Telnet; dedicated Telnet actions from row 14
No R2 prerequisite: session lifecycle entry points form the migration boundary; full recording-plus-transport acceptance requires both slices after integration.

title: Run serial sessions through the terminal-payload transport seam
what: Migrate the live serial session to the complete transport operations introduced for Telnet. A successfully configured COM port produces ordered payload and lifecycle facts through the same session consumer, while serial line control, BREAK and device-overrun behavior remain dedicated serial responsibilities.
criteria: Bind the session consumer before opening the port and keep required recording preparation before device I/O. Report readiness only after the configured COM port opens successfully; do not substitute a port or setting, infer remote login or add automatic reconnection.

Route serial receive, encoded input submission and disconnect through the common complete operations with the same source/order, complete-prefix/uncertainty and observation-versus-cancellation distinctions. Geometry reports that serial requires no wire notification rather than pretending to send one.

Preserve the selected flow-control and DTR/RTS ownership rules and dedicated BREAK operation, including its existing duration and cleanup attempt. Do not add a generic capabilities framework or change saved profile settings during temporary line operations.

Bound pending reads, payload, metadata, sends and late cleanup under existing accounting. Use supported flow control where it can recover, report device overrun explicitly, and never claim lossless backpressure or silently discard received payload.

Preserve received output and separately owned recording finalization across EOF/disconnect, cancelled waits, delayed port open/read/write/close and replacement generations. Actual device-resource release remains distinct from operation completion and visual removal.

Exercise the ordinary session/Rust/recording path with controlled serial adapters for partial writes, blocked consumers, overrun and late cancellation, and retain actual COM/device integration for driver behavior. Remove the serial caller's obsolete raw-wire recipe after migration.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q4-Q6: serial production adoption and dedicated device actions
Candidate 2 verification rows 1, 7, 9-14 as applicable to serial

title: Deliver SSH terminal startup and interaction through the shared transport and channel owners
what: Connect the SSH terminal path to the complete terminal-payload transport seam and the shared SSH channel owner first exercised by SFTP. Early DATA/stderr is processed before PTY/shell readiness, protocol control progresses during a slow terminal consumer or blocked send, and startup/closure results preserve the original session's output and resource ownership.
criteria: Bind the typed terminal consumer and current committed geometry before transport I/O; eliminate the SSH transport's dependency on constructing or calling a concrete terminal-session class. Reuse the shared channel owner for terminal open/PTY/shell/send/credit/close instead of copying its state, request or ownership machinery.

Preserve the existing host-trust, authentication, crypto and secret-lifetime owners. Deliver early DATA/stderr in source order while PTY/shell startup is pending, including output preceding refusal, timeout or cancellation; readiness follows protocol success and consumption of prior facts and never activates a stopped generation.

Use current dimensions when requesting the PTY after authentication/dialog delays. Coalesce subsequent startup geometry to the latest permitted notification without occupying the session reducer, and prevent stale geometry results from replacing current commitments.

Return eligible receive credit only after Rust processing, recording admission or its narrow failure, bounded reply admission and allocation release. Do not wait for generated-reply transmission, disk flush or painting; keep window adjustments, rekey and closure progressing with zero send credit or a held consumer.

Account advertised credit, outstanding reads, packed payload, source metadata and control work together. Verify more than 1,024 tiny alternating DATA/stderr messages and metadata-only pressure without unbounded item growth, silent loss or a healthy-looking deadlock; use recoverable pressure or the existing affected-session failure scope.

Use shared send outcomes to expose definitely submitted complete input units promptly for echo/pacing, preserve partial/uncertain suffixes without replay, and distinguish Stop Paste, abandoned observation and Disconnect. Preserve the existing unit boundaries supplied by the input owner, including the amended scalar/codec-safe Stop when that input slice is integrated.

Keep directional EOF and final cutoff separate. During the existing up-to-two-second peer-close grace, continue valid terminal delivery until channel/protocol/transport termination; do not treat late post-termination socket bytes as payload. EOF/closed facts hand off recording completion without awaiting it or claiming recording/retained-output release.

Startup failure and cancellation settle previously admitted delivery against its original generation. Consumer failure after partial mutation stops ordinary delivery without replay, false credit or dependence on a final closed callback; independent status reports the failure and actual resources stay owned through delayed I/O.

Verify the ordinary session/Rust/log path with controlled SSH packet/consumer/time/I/O schedules and real scripted-peer coverage for early output followed by failure, startup resize, zero-credit replies, rekey, partial sends, EOF with permitted reverse input and late generation cleanup. Exercise concurrent SFTP traffic to prove payload isolation and shared-writer progress, while retaining separate SFTP parsing/reopen acceptance.

Remove the obsolete session-facing raw read/acknowledge and concrete-session startup paths for SSH after its consumers migrate; preserve independent protocol vectors and the dedicated SFTP API. No external SSH client library or new terminal implementation is introduced.
coverage: Whole-codebase Q4-Q6: SSH production adoption and full bounded progress/failure contract
Whole-codebase Q17-Q19: terminal consumer of the shared SSH channel owner; S1/S2 own common writer/channel implementation
Candidate 2 verification rows 1-14 as applicable to SSH; transport closure and recording completion remain independent
